A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UNCHA study and contain complete main text, supplementary material, equations, figures, tables, and references. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original UNCHA benchmark results, component ablations, and embedding analyses in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v3 retains the original UNCHA experiments, including classification, retrieval, segmentation, box classification, and ablation results.

M1.justification: The uncertainty model, adaptive contrastive temperatures, entailment calibration, entropy regularization, and overall training objective in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: GRIT training and all evaluation coverage are retained, including classification, COCO/Flickr30K retrieval, compositional and part-level tests, VOC21 segmentation, and COCO/LVIS/OpenImages box classification.

E2.justification: CLIP, MERU, ATMG, and HyCoCLIP retain their corresponding comparison rows throughout the main and supplementary experiments. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the reported retrieval cutoffs from R@1/R@5 to R@5/R@10 for both directions on COCO and Flickr30K. This is a reported metric revision; the unchanged scores and generic recall@K descriptions do not establish reruns or changed experimental execution. Other settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 4, radius-surrogate ablation in Table S.6, hyperparameter analysis in Table S.11, and embedding, uncertainty, and localization analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting in the tables and analysis plots is unchanged. No run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes metric-value associations while retaining every score. For example, UNCHA ViT-S/16 COCO text-retrieval scores 69.9/79.7 are labeled R@1/R@5 in v1 and R@5/R@10 in v3. This is a reporting reassignment, not evidence of a same-setting performance change. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The Lorentz-space definitions and mathematical formulations in Equations 1–18, together with the radius/norm derivation in Equations S.19–S.27, are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims. Rephrasing the final introduction contribution bullet does not change its scientific meaning or scope.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting uncertainty calibration and entropy regularization to part-whole separation and compositional performance are retained. No substantive interpretation, applicability boundary, or limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: The supplementary architecture, initialization, hyperparameter, preprocessing, optimizer, hardware, and training details are identical. The abstract's code/model access statement and link are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 73 references and retain the same positioning relative to MERU, ATMG, HyCoCLIP, and uncertainty-based hyperbolic learning.

P1.justification: The final contribution bullet is shortened and its task list reordered. Section 2.2 drops 'space' from 'in hyperbolic space,' and the arXiv version/date changes. The remaining narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2's retrieval headers and column spacing change. Text reflow on pages 2–3 also separates the overlapping '3. Method' and '3.1. Preliminaries' headings visible in v1. Figures and supplementary layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 fixes the overlapping Section 3/3.1 headings, providing a small readability benefit. However, Table 2 relabels unchanged retrieval scores from R@1/R@5 to R@5/R@10 without explanation. Sections 4.2.2 and S.2.2.2 do not specify the evaluated K values independently, so the PDFs cannot establish whether this corrects or introduces misreporting. The overall quality effect therefore remains uncertain.
